Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In this topic, we'll practice solving systems of linear equations using elimination. This involves multiplying one or both equations by constant factors and then adding them to eliminate one of the variables.

Item 2 — Example: Solving a System by Premultiplying One Equation

Example Prompt:

The solution to the given system of equations is [MATH: (p, q).] What is the value of [MATH: pq?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We will solve the system using the elimination method.

Notice that if we multiply the second equation by [MATH: 2,] then we will get a [MATH: -6p] term that can cancel with the [MATH: 6p] term in the first equation:

[MATH: {6p − 7q = 2; − 3p + 4q = 5||× 2]

When we add the two equations, we obtain:
[MATH: 6p − 7q|= 2; − 6p + 8q|= 10; (− 7q + 8q)|= (2 + 10); q|= 12]

Now, substitute [MATH: q = 12] into one of the original equations to solve for [MATH: p.] We'll use the first equation:
[MATH: 6p − 7q|= 2; 6p − 7(12)|= 2; 6p − 84|= 2; 6p|= 86; p|= (43)/(3)]

Hence, we get
[MATH: pq = \dfrac{43}{3} \cdot 12 = 172.]
